summary: The main new story in this snapshot is SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS. It's a randomized trial of tirzepatide in teens aged 12 to 17, published in JAMA on 15 Nov. I checked the numbers: BMI fell 18.5% on tirzepatide and rose 0.5% on placebo over 72 weeks, and 48.1% of teens on the drug had a BMI drop of 20% or more. Cover it as a broad "what did the trial find?" piece for parents. The NEJM trial of semaglutide in children aged 6 to 11 can sit inside that video as context. The FDA's class-wide warning about the eye condition NAION (set 9 Nov) has now spread from trade press to consumer outlets (Good Housekeeping, Best Life and local TV on 17 Nov), so it is near peak. Our answer is the absolute risk: about 6.4 vs 3.8 cases per 100,000 people per year. The Washington Post's 16 Nov piece on "serious complications" gives the queued Serious Risks video a timely hook. Thanksgiving is 9 days away, so holiday-table Shorts (fullness, drinks, taking the pen when travelling) are at their best timing now. Coverage on 16–17 Nov in The Conversation, Medical Xpress and AllSci of "why GLP-1s don't work for everyone" (gene variants that affect semaglutide but not tirzepatide) points to a broad "Tirzepatide not working?" long video. Two other stories are hooks only, never the topic: the small UK nutrient-gap study (14 people) and the "heart risk after stopping" story (an observational March study of veterans, recirculating now). The brain/dementia review in Science gets a careful "what's proven" treatment, since semaglutide's Alzheimer's trials failed. Rejected: gray-market and "research" retatrutide, compounded GLP-1s, the stories about people staying on low doses or switching drugs, pricing, Medicare and coverage, and the mouse and animal pipeline studies. No new randomized head-to-head against tirzepatide in an obesity population has turned up from ObesityWeek. The EloraTZP data is from Sept–Oct, so it isn't a fresh trigger.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide for teens with obesity: SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS randomized trial (JAMA, 15 Nov 2026): BMI −18.5% vs +0.5% on placebo over 72 weeks, with semaglutide's NEJM trial in children aged 6 to 11 as context
candidates.angle: Long video: 'Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) for Teens: What Did the Trial Find?' A calm explainer for parents. Who was enrolled: ages 12–17 with obesity, or overweight plus at least one obesity-related complication, all also following a healthy-lifestyle programme. Results: BMI −18.5% vs +0.5% on placebo, and 48.1% of teens on tirzepatide had a BMI drop of 20% or more. Side effects: GI effects were common, according to Medical Daily, which also reports weight came back in the semaglutide children's trial after treatment stopped. Close with what this does and doesn't mean for families and the questions to bring to a paediatrician. No dosing, and say clearly that the US label approval status for under-18s must be checked on the day before publishing.
candidates.predicted_peak: 3–10 days (NYT, Bloomberg, Medscape and MedPage covered it; creator coverage still thin)
candidates.why_now: A peer-reviewed phase 3 RCT in JAMA (15 Nov) plus semaglutide's NEJM trial in children (16 Nov) means two major paediatric GLP-1 trials in 48 hours. The NYT is framing it around doctors' unease, which is the classic stage just before mainstream and creator pickup. Parents (25–55) are squarely in our audience.

evidence.signal: RCT published online 15 Nov: BMI −18.5% vs +0.5% placebo at 72 weeks; 48.1% had ≥20% BMI reduction
